description: ESG classification prompts for sportswear brand news articles

v1.0.0.commit_message: Initial prompt version - baseline extracted from config.py
v1.0.0.description: Original ESG labeling prompts with brand verification, ESG category definitions, and false positive guidance

v1.1.0.commit_message: Add Substantive Coverage Test for clearer false positive classification
v1.1.0.description: Adds explicit guidance for identifying false positives where brand mentions are too tangential to warrant inclusion in any topical category. Clarifies that articles with superficial brand references (data tables, roundup lists, passing mentions) should be marked as false positives.

v1.2.0.commit_message: Clarify is_sportswear_brand policy for stock articles
v1.2.0.description: Clarifies that is_sportswear_brand is about substantive content, not just identity. Pure stock metrics (short interest, price movements, moving averages) with no commentary should be false_positive. Adds Finance Category Test: would this article be useful if we added a Finance category? If just raw metrics from Yahoo Finance, it's a false positive.

v1.3.0.commit_message: Add comprehensive product review guidance to prevent ESG mislabeling
v1.3.0.description: Adds critical section distinguishing product reviews, roundups, shopping articles, gift guides, and sneaker drops from corporate ESG news. Product content that mentions sustainable materials should NOT receive ESG categories - sustainability features are product marketing copy, not corporate ESG reporting. Includes examples table, key question test, and guidance on borderline product launches with ESG angle.

v1.4.0.commit_message: Add explicit guidance for comparison/analogy brand mentions as false positives
v1.4.0.description: Adds detailed guidance for identifying false positives when brands are mentioned only as comparisons, analogies, or reference points. New section covers color comparisons ('reminiscent of Nike's Infrared'), style comparisons ('Patagonia vibes'), quality references ('rivals Under Armour'), and aspiration analogies ('the Patagonia of baby clothes'). Includes quick-check question to help distinguish between articles ABOUT a brand vs articles using the brand as a reference point. Addresses cases like the Herman Miller gaming chair article that mentioned Nike only as a color comparison.

v1.5.0.commit_message: Stricter governance criteria - decision tree and extensive negative examples
v1.5.0.description: Major update to prevent governance mislabeling. Adds decision tree for governance classification, extensive table of examples that should NOT receive governance labels (stock prices, earnings, analyst opinions, executive appointments, investments), and explicit 'critical test' for governance. Addresses EP classifier data quality issue where ~50% of ESG labels were governance-only articles that were actually financial news.

v1.6.0.commit_message: Stricter Environmental and Social criteria - decision trees and negative examples
v1.6.0.description: Major update to prevent Environmental and Social mislabeling. Environmental: Adds decision tree clarifying that mentioning sustainable materials in product descriptions is NOT Environmental ESG - the article must be ABOUT the sustainability initiative, not just mention it as a product feature. Product reviews, shopping articles, and gift guides should never receive Environmental labels. Social: Adds decision tree and extensive examples for avoiding mislabeling store openings (retail news), celebrity endorsements (marketing), athlete sponsorships (business), and fashion events (lifestyle) as Social. Also adds Mizuno brand verification guidance to prevent false positives when articles mention actress Sonoya Mizuno rather than Mizuno sportswear.

v1.7.0.commit_message: Stricter financial article classification with extensive examples
v1.7.0.description: Major expansion of is_sportswear_brand guidance for financial articles. Addresses persistent mislabeling of auto-generated stock articles (13F filings, institutional holdings, short interest, moving averages, boilerplate analyst roundups, stock comparisons) as sportswear when they should be false positives. Adds 30+ specific real-world examples organized by article type: institutional holdings templates, stock price/volume articles, short interest updates, boilerplate analyst rating roundups, stock comparison tables, auto-generated return calculators, and shopping/deals articles. Clarifies the decision boundary: human-written analysis or commentary = sportswear, auto-generated template content = false positive. Based on review of 129 mislabeled articles in training data.

v1.8.0.commit_message: Omit brands with no applicable ESG categories from response
v1.8.0.description: Strengthens user prompt instruction to omit sportswear brands that have no applicable ESG categories (all categories would be applies: false). Previously the prompt said to omit brands with 'no substantive ESG content' but Claude sometimes still included them with all-false labels. Now uses explicit CRITICAL instruction with example scenario (brand mentioned only as competitor/reference). Also adds defensive filter in save_brand_labels() to skip brands with empty label sets.

v1.9.0.commit_message: Migrate labeling model to Claude Sonnet 4.6
v1.9.0.description: Identical prompt text to v1.8.0; updates the recommended model to claude-sonnet-4-6 following the retirement of claude-sonnet-4-20250514. Validated by a retrospective contrastive eval (issue #38): re-labeling 299 already-labeled articles with Sonnet 4.6 on the v1.8.0 prompt showed 0% newly-labeled rate (no scorecard-inflation risk), 0 parse failures, 92.4% exact sentiment agreement, and outcome disagreements dominated by 4.6 correctly rejecting brand-name-collision false positives (e.g. 'forensic vans', 'pumas in Patagonia') that Sonnet 4 mislabeled.
